Published online:
    September 1, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]

Synopsis:
    US manufacturing PMI dipped to 54.6 in August from 55.6 in July, missing the 55.2 forecast but remaining in expansion territory. New orders softened, factory employment slipped, and supply chain pressures persisted — with supplier deliveries slowing further. Input prices held firm at 71.1, keeping inflation well above the Fed's 2% target. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signaled more tightening may be needed if inflation does not convincingly trend toward target. Markets are pricing a ~70% probability of a 25bps hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (Core themes are US manufacturing health, inflationary pressure, and Fed rate policy)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (strongly directional toward a hike given sticky input prices, hawkish Warsh commentary, and market pricing)
Probability of increase: 70%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 15 (softening PMI and new orders provide a minor counter-narrative but are not the dominant signal)
Probability of holding: 30%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (no dovish pivot signal anywhere in the article)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 65 (More hawkish than before — sticky input prices at 71.1 unchanged, Warsh explicitly warning of "work to do," and ~70% market-implied probability of a September hike all point to a clearly hawkish near-term stance; the modest PMI miss provides only marginal softening)
